solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amusing chap travelling by rail or older form of transport

parts.note: a wag is a joker, an amusing fellow
someone travelling by rail is on a train

explanation.surface: A comedian takes the train, or some quainter old conveyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers crossing the American West travelled in convoys of covered wagons, an old way of moving people and goods.

clue.text: Wife that is most broad

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: The wife, it seems, is the broadest of them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Widest is the superlative of wide, a straightforward synonym of broad.

clue.text: Nonsense gets a weak laugh

parts.note: guff is informal for nonsense or empty talk

explanation.surface: Silly talk earns only a feeble chuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a loud hearty laugh, a particular kind of laughter.

clue.text: Cruelly harm lean tanned primitive type

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the words are treated roughly, so their letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone viciously injures a slim, sunburnt caveman.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct early human species, the archetype of a primitive, brutish person.

clue.text: Harry Lauder ran as church dignitary

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are pushed around; it also poses as the singer's first name

explanation.surface: The Scottish entertainer Harry Lauder stood as a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish music-hall singer, so 'Harry' reads as his name, not the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is an Anglican cleric who oversees a group of parishes, a church office.

clue.text: Keys for passageways by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for passageways is heard, not spelt

parts.note: aisles are passageways between rows of seats

explanation.surface: Piano keys stand in for corridors, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' are low islands, as in the Florida Keys, not things that open locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a small low island, so keys are islands.

clue.text: Northerner one's excluded from racecourse

indicators.note: being excluded from means being shut out of the racecourse word, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire
one is A, the indefinite article as a number

explanation.surface: A northern racegoer finds himself barred from the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' drops A from ASCOT, the Berkshire racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, the northernmost nation of Britain, so is a northerner to the English.

clue.text: Yields to falsehood in 'bog-standard' schools

indicators.note: in means the falsehood word sits inside the schools word

parts.note: comps is short for comprehensive schools, the UK state secondary schools
a lie is a falsehood

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to a lie told in ordinary state schools.
explanation.walkthrough: Comprehensives are British non-selective state secondary schools; 'bog-standard comprehensive' was a notorious political phrase, so the quoted words decorate the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield to a request or rule is to comply with it.

clue.text: Officers to lead donkey's about right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the lead and donkey words go round the letter for right

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
an ass is a donkey; the 's is donkey is

explanation.surface: To lead a donkey is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is a colloquial term for high-ranking military officers.

clue.text: HP Lovecraft's foremost with world of fantasy

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, called the never-never in Britain

indicators.note: foremost asks for the first letter of the author's name

parts.note: and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: H.P. Lovecraft's chief work has a fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: H.P. Lovecraft was a horror writer, but here HP is hire purchase, buying in instalments, which British slang calls the 'never-never'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's island is the archetypal imaginary place, so the name means any idealised fantasy realm.

clue.text: Almost settle the country's ministry

indicators.note: almost means the word for settle falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to defray a bill or cost is to settle it

explanation.surface: A government department nearly pays up what it owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter Y from DEFRAY. DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Defra is the acronym of a British government department, the ministry for environment, food and rural affairs.

clue.text: Gather about stormy life with Master, it has its ups and downs

definitions.text: it has its ups and downs

indicators.note: about means the word for gather is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of life are thrown into a new order

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for Master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: Gather round a turbulent life with your master; such is existence, with its highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a map showing terrain in raised form literally has ups and downs.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows hills and valleys in raised form, so it literally has ups and downs.

clue.text: Look over boy turning in disgrace

parts.note: to scan something is to look over it

indicators.note: turning means the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Examining a youth who has gone to the bad brings shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a shameful event that brings public disgrace on those involved.

clue.text: More dandified servant of S Pickwick

definitions.meaning: comparative of swell, a fashionable dandy, so smarter and more showily dressed
Samuel Pickwick's manservant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers is Sam Weller

explanation.surface: A flashier dresser waits on Mr Pickwick.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S WELLER: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is an old word for a fashionable dandy, and the comparative describes someone smarter still.

clue.text: Cultivating talent adds spice to keeping wild fern round Spain

indicators.note: keeping means the spice word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: to ginger something is to spice it up

indicators.note: round means the scrambled fern goes around the letter for Spain
wild signals the letters of fern are scrambled

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A gardener's gift spices things up by tending wild ferns around Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivating talent' is the British idiom for a gift for gardening; Spain's E comes from vehicle registration codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a knack for growing plants is said to have a gift for cultivation, a British idiom.

clue.text: Without a care, such infancy would be fashionable

parts.note: take the word infancy and free it of its fancy: what remains is the two-letter word meaning fashionable

explanation.surface: Being carefree, a childhood like that would be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: 'infancy' with 'fancy' removed leaves IN, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fancy-free is not in love or committed, and so has no cares.

clue.text: Spy girl in year out

indicators.note: in means the girl word sits inside the anagram
out means the letters of year are put out of place

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl

explanation.surface: A secret agent's girlfriend is away for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' is the definition, not the verb; an envoy on a secret mission fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, sometimes a secret one, so a spy.

clue.text: What's made finally in working at craft

definitions.text: What's made finally in working at craft

indicators.note: in means that final letter goes inside the scrambled words
working suggests the letters are worked into a new order
finally asks for the last letter of made

explanation.surface: An object is what results when craft is put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: something made by working with craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human skill, the product of craftsmanship.

clue.text: Irregular army can then capture five ships

indicators.note: capture means the anagram closes round the numeral
irregular says the letters of the following words are put out of order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Guerrilla soldiers manage to seize five vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular army' reads as guerrillas, but 'Irregular' is the anagram signal and 'ships' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's commercial shipping fleet, as opposed to its warships, is a collective name for trading vessels.

clue.text: Some of the drowsiest animals rest

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the sleepiest creatures take a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a period of rest.

clue.text: Representation of person well-regarded in country

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the country word

parts.note: a state is a country
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, hence well-regarded

explanation.surface: An image of a respected figure in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage, as opposed to non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, often a likeness of a particular person.

clue.text: The girl has to make a visit returning clobber

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

indicators.note: returning means the visiting word is read backwards

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: A woman pops round to return some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses CALL to LLAC. 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes, but here it is the verb to beat thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To shellac someone is informal for thrashing or defeating them heavily, the same as to clobber.

clue.text: Bag fastening

definitions.meaning: to bag is to ... or capture, as a hunter does
a device such as a latch that holds something shut

explanation.definitionFit: To bag game is to capture it, and a door latch is a fastener; both are senses of one word.

clue.text: Civil war protagonist arrayed in rosy kit

indicators.note: arrayed means set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier of an old civil war is dressed in rose-coloured gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were fifteenth-century English civil wars between the houses of York (white rose) and Lancaster (red rose), hence the apt 'rosy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the House of York was one side in the Wars of the Roses, England's dynastic civil war.

clue.text: An experimental flower maybe pure white

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A
lab, short for laboratory, is used adjectivally for experimental work
an aster is one example of a flower

explanation.surface: A new experimental bloom might be perfectly white.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white stone, so the word describes skin or surfaces that are pure white.

clue.text: Something valuable when regulated

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
set means fixed or regulated, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A prized item when it is controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is property or a quality of worth, a thing that is valuable to its owner.

clue.text: Unknown alien, one supposed highland inhabitant

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like X
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film E.T.
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mysterious extraterrestrial is thought to live in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highland' is the Himalayas, not the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a creature said, without proof, to live high in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Study lawyers in the case that's falling apart

indicators.note: in means the study and lawyer words go inside the outer word

parts.note: the word the serves as the case or container
to read a subject is to study it, especially at university
the Bar is the collective term for barristers

explanation.surface: Examining the legal profession's case shows it is collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn so thin that it is coming to pieces.
